literal: The letter 'A' having as beginning letters all, the primordial Divine having as beginning indeed the world.
translation: As all letters have the letter 'A' as their starting point, so the world has the primordial Divine as its beginning.
modern: எழுத்துக்கள் எல்லாம் அகரத்தை முதலாகக் கொண்டுள்ளன; அதுபோல, இந்த உலகம் ஆதி பகவானை முதலாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.
explanation: This opening couplet of the Tirukkuṟaḷ establishes a profound analogy between language and existence. Just as the sound 'A' (அகர) is the fundamental, inherent starting point of all written and spoken letters (எழுத்து எல்லாம்), the primordial Divine (ஆதி பகவன்) is the source and origin of the entire universe (உலகு). The word 'முதற்றே' uses an emphatic suffix to stress that the world's existence is absolutely dependent on this primary source, just as speech depends on its first sound.
